seed: Objects of type `block` under action ACTION1 with touching neighbours [portal] show mixed outcomes: no_change x26, y x1, w,x,y x1, h,w,x,y x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the exact click position relative to the object, when the action is a click. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Player moves 3 per arrow (1 up,2 down,3 left,4 right) unless blocked by a hidden wall; a block touching the player on that side is kicked instead (player stays).
Kicked block slides 3/step, chaining blocks it runs into, until wall/bounds/player/non-fitting socket interior blocks the chain (fitting-socket stop unobserved).
Click (action 6) on a block: it becomes the player (player takes its rect), old player vanishes; blocks renamed token_i by (y,x).
Portal has no pixels, so walls are invisible: inferred wall rects (27,54,3,3) and (33,27,12,3) are level-specific constants.
The block A1 portal-touch hypothesis was a red herring (the portal bbox touches everything): the outcome depends on whether the player is adjacent below the block. Passes stateless.
